answer: A verifiable delay protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to compute sequential, non-parallelizable cryptographic steps along a state chain that extends like a vine. Calibrated against quartz clock frequencies, each proof forces an attacker to expend scarce single-threaded processor time and electricity per identity, meaning forged nodes accumulate as slowly as a glacier. However, this imposes continuous energy waste on honest participants and excludes low-power edge devices.
